title: Rabbah bar Rav Nachman
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Shabbat 119a and Chullin 111a: Rabbah son of Rav Huna visited the house of Rabbah bar Rav Nachman; he brought before him three se’ah of cakes. He said to him: “Did you know I was coming?” He said to him: “Are you preferable to us over it (over Shabbat)?” … Meanwhile he found a liver whose duct had absorbed blood, and he instructed them how to proceed.

In Menachot 41a: Rabbah son of Rav Huna visited him and saw that Rava bar Rav Nachman was covered with a folded cloak; he said to him, “Is this not a corner?” … and he said to Rava bar Rav Nachman, “Do you think it is an obligation of the person?” etc. Hyman infers from this that Rabbah son of Rav Huna was greater than he, and so it is according to the chronology, for Rabbah son of Rav Huna was the colleague of Rav Chisda, the colleague of Rav Nachman, while Rabbah bar Rav Nachman was Rav Nachman’s son. Even so we find in Yevamot 25 that once Rabbah son of Rav Huna sent him a law to clarify and wrote to him in the language “Let our master teach us.” Hyman explains this by noting that, as is known, Rabbah son of Rav Huna was very humble; moreover it is possible because once Rabbah bar Rav Nachman passed by in a ship, saw a forest on the bank of the river and ordered it cut down; the forest belonged to Rabbah son of Rav Huna, and Rabbah son of Rav Huna cursed whoever cut his forest that his offspring should not survive. So it was: all the days of Rabbah son of Rav Huna, the offspring of Rabbah bar Rav Nachman did not survive, as in Bava Metzia 108a. He therefore suggests it is possible that he wrote to him “Let our master teach us” in order to appease him.
He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Orlah 2:3 as Abba son of Rav Nachman.
In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:3: Rabbi Acha in the name of Rabbi Abba bar Rav Nachman.

In Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1, folio 31a: Rabbah bar Nachman in the name of Rabbi Berekhyah. Hyman suspects a scribal error, for they said there: “Until when did the merit of the fathers endure? Rabbi Tanchuma said to him in the name of Rabbi Chiyya; Rabbah bar Nachman said to him in the name of Rabbi Berekhyah,” etc. Hyman proposes: “Rabbi Tanchuma said to him in the name of Rabbi Chiyya Rabbah; Rabbi Nachman said to him in the name of Rabbi Berekhyah.”

notes.text: The liver’s סמפון is a duct, not a lung bronchus. The father/son chronology refers to Rabbah barNachman as Nachman’s son, not Rabbah barHuna. ומנחתו/וען/ומ״ל are read as Menachot/וכן/ונ״ל as disclosed previously. Rava/Rabbah, Abba and ChiyyaRabbah/RabbiNachman repartition remain explicit Hyman textual arguments, not silently harmonized.

The consulted Chullin 111a continues the visit with a liver duct containing blood and the instruction to cut lengthwise and crosswise, cut side downward. This is not a bronchus. Rabbah bar Nachman is Nachman’s son, not Huna’s. The body retains Rava/Rabbah and Abba variants, Hyman’s chronology, the forest-curse appeasement conjecture and his Chiyya Rabbah/Nachman repartition without a new identity merger.
